answer: Divergent Challenge Ladder. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge within one pulse, and answers are committed to a shared log. Clones cannot diverge: identical copies produce identical answers, so the system forks their histories at a river junction and requires provably distinct responses downstream. An attacker cloning one agent pays a full independent response cost per copy, plus a delta penalty whenever two copies answer alike, making N clones cost more than N separate agents.
